title: Suspected intravascular large B-cell lymphoma (IVLBCL)
consultQuestion: Progressive multifocal infarcts or encephalopathy with nonspecific MRI, high LDH, or unexplained fever — intravascular lymphoma? Skin biopsy before brain biopsy?
keyHistory: Neurologic findings in 75–76%, constitutional symptoms (fever, sweats, weight loss), skin lesions (Rozenbaum)
Fever of unknown origin; HLH features (HLH mostly in the Asian variant) (Rozenbaum; Shimada)
keyExam: Skin: plaques, nodules, violaceous patches, petechiae, telangiectasias, cherry angiomas (Rozenbaum)
redFlags: Rapidly progressive course — aggressive lymphoma with poor prognosis (Shimada)
Neurological symptoms with unrevealing imaging — imaging detects CNS involvement in only about half (Shimada)

clues: Imaging can be identical (Shimada); 25% of patients biopsied for IVL who didn't have it had CNS vasculitis (Rozenbaum)

notes: LDH raised in 10/11 Western patients (Rozenbaum), 104/106 (98%) in a Japanese cohort and 69% in a European series (Shimada)
sIL-2R >5000 U/mL in 63/96 (66%) of a Japanese cohort, significantly higher in Asian-variant than non-Asian IVLBCL — yield in Western patients not reported (Shimada)
≥3 sites of normal-appearing skin plus any skin lesions and cherry angiomas; 4-mm punch deep enough to include subcutaneous fat (Rozenbaum)
Sensitivity 50% (12 cases), specificity 100%; positive in 1 of 10 patients evaluated (Rozenbaum)
Lesional skin more sensitive than uninvolved skin (67% vs 33%) (Rozenbaum)
Nonspecific white-matter hyperintensity that can mimic small-vessel disease, demyelination, or vasculitis (Shimada)
Negative in all 9 Western patients who had it (Rozenbaum); intrasinusoidal involvement is common in Asian series and repeat biopsy may help (Shimada)

indication: Skin biopsies negative and suspicion persists
notes: 6 of 12 IVL cases in Rozenbaum were diagnosed by other means, typically brain biopsy

decisionRules.recommendation: Random skin biopsies (≥3 normal-skin sites + lesions + angiomas, deep with fat) before brain biopsy
evidenceNote: Rozenbaum 2021: authors' suggested approach; skin-before-brain order not tested
Shimada 2009: random skin biopsy promising, data still limited

initialSteps: Hematology/oncology once suspected — adding rituximab to chemotherapy has shown benefit (Shimada)
institutionVaries: Dermatology availability for multiple deep punch biopsies
pearls: Very low HDL may be a clue (median 23 mg/dL; 2 patients <5) (Rozenbaum)
Random skin biopsy can be positive even where the cutaneous variant is rare (Shimada)
sources: Rozenbaum D, et al. Skin biopsy in the diagnosis of intravascular lymphoma: A retrospective diagnostic accuracy study. J Am Acad Dermatol 2021;85:665-670. doi:10.1016/j.jaad.2019.09.015
Shimada K, Kinoshita T, Naoe T, Nakamura S. Presentation and management of intravascular large B-cell lymphoma. Lancet Oncol 2009;10:895-902
